mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts (HOUST) above 550K units signals strengthening consumer demand, leading to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when HOUST > 550K, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 0.5%) signals accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, regardless of other market conditions.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when FEDFUNDS < 0.5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises by more than 0.5pp in 2 months, it signals labor market weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, especially if payroll employment (PAYEMS) growth slows concurrently.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5pp in 2mo, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 6-month moving average signals strengthening supply chains, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when INDPRO > 6mo MA are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in real personal savings (RSAFS) below $300B signals increased consumer spending, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days, especially during holiday seasons.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 50% of instances when RSAFS < $300B during holiday seasons, or Rank IC < 0.01 over any 1-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) move in opposite directions over 3 months, it signals monetary policy mismatch, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL move in opposite directions over 3mo
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL move in opposite directions over 3mo, or Rank IC < 0.025 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 5%) signals a tight labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days, as companies invest in growth initiatives to attract and retain talent.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns when UNRATE < 5% are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds 3% YoY and housing starts (HOUST) are above 500K units, it signals robust demand, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days, as both consumer and business spending drive economic growth.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 50% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 3% YoY and HOUST > 500K, or Rank IC < 0.02 over any 1.5-year rolling window.
